content: 1. Lovastatin increases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Close monitoring is recommended to avoid potential adverse effects. 2. Lumefantrine decreases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. 3. Bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens reduce magnesium chloride levels by shifting magnesium from the bloodstream to tissue storage. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 4. Bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens reduce magnesium citrate levels through a similar mechanism, shifting magnesium to tissue storage. The clinical significance remains unclear, and monitoring is recommended. 5. Bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens reduce magnesium hydroxide levels by shifting magnesium from the blood to tissue storage. The clinical impact is uncertain, and monitoring is advised. 6. Bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens reduce magnesium oxide levels by increasing tissue storage of magnesium. The clinical significance is unknown, and monitoring is recommended. 7. Bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens reduce magnesium sulfate levels by shifting magnesium to tissue storage. The clinical relevance of this interaction is unclear, and monitoring is advised. 8. Bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens may interact with maprotiline through an unspecified mechanism. Estrogens and progestins may reduce the therapeutic effects of tricyclic antidepressants while increasing plasma concentrations and adverse effects. Close monitoring is necessary. 9. Bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens increase maraviroc levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism in the liver and intestines. This interaction may increase the risk of toxicity, and close monitoring is required. 10. Marijuana increases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is recommended to prevent adverse effects. 11. Meropenem decreases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 12. Meropenem/vaborbactam also decreases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction is specific to oral hormone forms and has a low risk of contraceptive failure. Monitoring is recommended. 13. Methylprednisolone decreases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism in the liver and intestines. Close monitoring is necessary. 14. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. However, it may also decrease the levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral hormone forms and has a low risk of contraceptive failure. Monitoring is advised. 15. Bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens reduce metyrapone effects through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is recommended. 16. Miconazole vaginal increases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is necessary. 17. Minocycline decreases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral hormone forms and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Monitoring is advised. 18. Moxifloxacin decreases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction is specific to oral hormone forms and has a low risk of contraceptive failure. Monitoring is recommended. 19. Mycophenolate reduces the effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens through an unknown mechanism. The clinical significance is unclear, and monitoring is advised. 20. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral hormone forms and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Monitoring is necessary.
